title: Second Half Heavier
description: Split `a` in the middle: the first half has the first `floor(n / 2)` elements and the second half has the rest (so the middle element of an odd-length array belongs to the second half). Return `true` if the second half has a strictly larger sum than the first.

title: Fixed Point Count
description: Return the number of indices `i` with `a[i] == i` (indices start at `0`).

title: Every Kth Sum
description: Return the sum of the elements of `a` at positions `k, 2k, 3k, ...` counting from `1` (that is, the indices `k-1, 2k-1, ...`).

title: Last Index Of Minimum
description: Return the largest index at which the smallest value of `a` occurs.

examples.explanation: The last minimum is at index 3.
The last minimum is at index 0.

title: Neighbour Sum Matches
description: Return how many inner elements `a[i]` (with `0 < i < n - 1`) are equal to the sum of their two neighbours `a[i - 1] + a[i + 1]`.

title: Largest Adjacent Sum
description: Return the largest value of `a[i] + a[i + 1]` over all neighbouring pairs of `a`.

title: Rotated First Element
description: Rotate `a` to the left by `k` positions (the first `k` elements move to the end; `k` may exceed the length). Return the first element of the rotated array.

title: Greater Than Last Count
description: Return how many elements of `a` are strictly greater than its last element.

title: Missing From One To N
description: Return how many of the integers `1, 2, ..., n` do not appear in `a`.

title: Extra Duplicate Count
description: Return how many elements of `a` are repeats of a value that already appeared earlier in `a` (the total length minus the number of different values).

title: Clamped Total
description: Replace every element of `a` below `lo` by `lo` and every element above `hi` by `hi`. Return the sum of the resulting values.

title: Even Squares Sum
description: Return the sum of the squares of the even elements of `a`.

title: Descent Count
description: Return the number of positions `i` with `a[i] > a[i + 1]`.

title: Largest Neighbour Jump
description: Return the largest value of `|a[i] - a[i + 1]|` over all neighbouring pairs of `a`.

title: Arithmetic Progression Check
description: Return `true` if the consecutive differences of `a` are all equal (arrays with one or two elements count as progressions).

title: Even Sum Neighbour Pairs
description: Return how many neighbouring pairs `(a[i], a[i + 1])` have an even sum.

title: Vowel Start Word Count
description: `s` is a sentence of lowercase words separated by single spaces. Return how many words start with a vowel (`a`, `e`, `i`, `o`, `u`).
constraints: s has lowercase words separated by single spaces, with no leading or trailing space

title: Last Word Length
description: `s` consists of lowercase letters and spaces and has at least one letter. Return the length of its last word (a maximal block of letters); spaces may follow it.
constraints: s has lowercase letters and spaces and contains at least one letter

title: Sorted Letters Check
description: Return `true` if the letters of `s` are in non-decreasing alphabetical order from left to right.

title: Words Of Length K
description: `s` is a sentence of lowercase words separated by single spaces. Return how many words have exactly `k` letters.

examples.input: s = "the cat sat on a mat", k = 3

constraints: s has lowercase words separated by single spaces, with no leading or trailing space

args: the cat sat on a mat

title: Same Letter Substring Count
description: Return the number of non-empty substrings of `s` made of one repeated letter. Substrings at different positions count separately (for `aaa` the answer is `6`).

title: Top Letter Count
description: Return how many times the most frequent letter of `s` occurs.

title: Length Without Vowels
description: Return the length of `s` after deleting every vowel (`a`, `e`, `i`, `o`, `u`).

title: Swap Adjacent Letters
description: Swap the letters at positions `0` and `1`, then at `2` and `3`, and so on. If the length is odd the last letter stays. Return the resulting string.

title: Cyclic Repeat To Length
description: Write `s` over and over (cycling back to its start) and return the first `n` characters of the result.

title: Shared Letter Count
description: Return the largest number of letters that can be matched one-to-one between `s` and `t` (each letter of `s` is matched with an equal letter of `t`, each letter used at most once).
constraints: s and t have only lowercase letters

title: Next Multiple Above
description: Return the smallest multiple of `m` that is strictly greater than `n`.

title: Sum Of Cubes Upto
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Powers Of Two Upto N
description: Return how many powers of two (`1, 2, 4, 8, ...`) are less than or equal to `n`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Perfect Cube Check
description: Return `true` if `n` is a perfect cube (`k * k * k` for some integer `k >= 0`).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Gcd Of Array
description: Return the greatest common divisor of all elements of `a`.

title: Least Common Multiple Of Two
description: Return the least common multiple of `a` and `b`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Odd Position Digit Sum
description: Number the digits of `n` from the right starting at `1`. Return the sum of the digits at the odd positions (`1`, `3`, `5`, ...).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Small Binomial
description: Return the number of ways to choose `k` items from `n` items, `C(n, k)`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Halving Steps To Zero
description: Starting from `n`, repeatedly replace it by `floor(n / 2)`. Return how many replacements are needed to reach `0`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Profit From At Most K Trades
description: `a[i]` is a share price on day `i`. A trade buys one share on some day and sells it on a later day; you can hold at most one share at a time (a new trade may start only after the previous one was sold, possibly on the same day it was sold) and make at most `k` trades. Return the largest total profit.

title: Ways With At Most K Coins
description: You have unlimited coins of each value in `coins`. Return the number of different multisets of coins (the order does not matter) with total value exactly `amount` that use at most `k` coins in total, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: 1 <= coins.length <= 10, coins are distinct values in 1..1000

title: Queens Placements Count
description: Return the number of ways to place `n` chess queens on an `n x n` board so that no two queens attack each other (no two share a row, a column or a diagonal).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Best Tree Path Sum
description: A tree has nodes `0..n-1` with `n = par.length + 1`; node `i + 1` is joined to node `par[i]` (with `par[i] <= i`). Node `u` holds `vals[u]`, which may be negative. A path is a sequence of different nodes in which consecutive nodes are joined by an edge, and it may start and end anywhere (it has at least one node). Return the largest sum of node values along a path.

title: Kth Ancestor Total
description: A rooted tree has nodes `0..n-1` with `n = par.length + 1` and root `0`; node `i + 1` has parent `par[i]` (with `par[i] <= i`). `queries` lists questions as flat pairs `(node, k)`: the answer is the ancestor of `node` that is `k` steps up toward the root, or `-1` if the root is reached earlier. Return the sum of all answers, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The answers add up to 1 modulo 1000000007.
The answers add up to 0 modulo 1000000007.

constraints: 0 <= par.length <= 100000 and 2 <= queries.length <= 200000 and queries.length is even
0 <= par[i] <= i, 0 <= node <= par.length and 0 <= k <= 100000

title: Second Shortest Route Length
description: An undirected weighted graph has nodes `0..n-1`; `edges` lists roads as flat triples `(u, v, length)`. A route from node `0` to node `n - 1` may reuse roads and nodes. Return the length of the second shortest route, defined as the smallest route length that is strictly larger than the shortest one, or `-1` if node `n - 1` cannot be reached.

examples.explanation: The second shortest route has length 8.
The second shortest route has length 9.

constraints: 2 <= n <= 100000 and edges.length is a multiple of 3 and edges.length <= 300000

title: Added Edges For Strong Connectivity
description: A directed graph has nodes `0..n-1` and edges given as flat pairs `(from, to)` in `edges`. You may add new directed edges between existing nodes. Return the smallest number of edges to add so that every node can reach every other node.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= edges.length <= 200000 and edges.length is even

title: Shortest Front-Padded Palindrome Length
description: You may add letters only at the front of `s`. Return the length of the shortest palindrome you can obtain this way.

title: Longest Repeated Substring Length
description: Return the length of the longest substring that occurs at least twice in `s` (the two occurrences may overlap), or `0` if every substring occurs once.

examples.explanation: The longest repeated substring has 3 letters.
The longest repeated substring has 0 letters.

title: Anagram Substring Pairs
description: Count the pairs of substrings of `s` that have the same length, start at different positions, and are anagrams of each other (one is a rearrangement of the other). A pair is counted once, whatever the order of its two substrings.

title: Fewest Replacements To Increase
description: You may replace any element of `a` by any value taken from `b` (a value of `b` may be used for several replacements). Return the smallest number of replacements that makes `a` strictly increasing, or `-1` if that is impossible.

title: Best Block Sum One Deletion
description: Choose a contiguous part of `a` and then delete at most one element from it, so that at least one element remains. Return the largest possible sum of the remaining elements.

title: Shortest Subarray Sum At Least K
description: Return the length of the shortest non-empty contiguous part of `a` whose sum is at least `k`, or `-1` if there is none. Elements may be negative.

title: Minimum Starting Health Path
description: `g` is a grid stored row by row with `cols` columns; entering a cell changes your health by its value (negative values hurt, the starting cell also counts). You start in the top-left cell and walk to the bottom-right cell moving only right or down. Your health must be at least `1` after every cell. Return the smallest starting health that allows a valid walk.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 10000 and g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Return To Start Walk Count
description: A pointer starts at index `0` of an array of length `arrLen`. In each of `steps` steps it moves one place left, one place right, or stays, and it may never leave the array. Return the number of different move sequences after which the pointer is back at index `0`, modulo `1000000007`.

title: Equal Support Max Height
description: You have rods of lengths `a` and may weld some of them into two separate supports (each rod is used in at most one support, or left unused) so that both supports have exactly the same total length. Return the largest possible length of one support, or `0` if no non-empty equal pair of supports can be made.
constraints: 1 <= a[i] <= 1000 and the sum of all rods is at most 5000

title: Events Attendable Count
description: `events` lists events as flat pairs `(start, end)`; an event can be attended on any single day from `start` to `end`, both included. You can attend at most one event per day. Return the largest number of events you can attend.

title: Capital After K Projects
description: You start with capital `w` and may complete at most `k` different projects. Project `i` needs at least `capital[i]` capital to start and adds `profits[i]` to your capital when finished (the start requirement is not spent). Return the largest capital you can have at the end.

title: Kth In Row Column Sorted Grid
description: `g` is a grid stored row by row with `cols` columns in which every row is in non-decreasing order from left to right and every column is in non-decreasing order from top to bottom. Return the `k`-th smallest value among all cells (counting equal values separately, `k` starting from `1`).
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 10000 and g.length is a multiple of cols; rows and columns are sorted

title: Digit One Occurrences
description: Return how many times the digit `1` appears when all the integers from `1` to `n` are written in decimal (for example `11` contributes two), modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Segmented Prime Count
description: Return how many prime numbers lie in the range `[l, r]` (both ends included).

examples.explanation: There are 6 primes in the range.
There are 0 primes in the range.

title: Submatrices Divisible By K
description: `g` is a table stored row by row with `cols` columns. Count the rectangular blocks (consecutive rows and consecutive columns, at least one cell) whose sum is divisible by `k`. Return the count modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 2500 and g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Max XOR With Query Limit
description: `queries` lists questions as flat pairs `(x, m)`. The answer to a question is the largest value of `x XOR a[i]` over all elements with `a[i] <= m`, or `-1` if no element is that small. Return the sum of all answers, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The answers add up to 13 modulo 1000000007.
The answers add up to 4 modulo 1000000007.

constraints: 1 <= a.length <= 100000 and 2 <= queries.length <= 200000 and queries.length is even

title: Dice Sum Ways
description: Roll `d` dice, each with faces numbered `1..f`. Return the number of different outcomes (sequences of face values, so the dice are distinguishable) whose sum is exactly `target`, modulo `1000000007`.

title: Fewest Swaps To Palindrome
description: In one move you swap two neighbouring letters of `s`. Return the fewest moves needed to turn `s` into a palindrome. It is guaranteed that `s` can be rearranged into a palindrome.

examples.explanation: The fewest number of swaps is 2.
The fewest number of swaps is 0.

constraints: s has only lowercase letters and some rearrangement of s is a palindrome

title: Shortest Unsorted Stretch
description: Find the shortest contiguous part of `a` such that sorting only that part (in non-decreasing order) makes the whole array sorted. Return its length, or `0` if `a` is already sorted.

title: Except Self Product Total
description: For each index `i`, let `p[i]` be the product of all elements of `a` except `a[i]`. Return the sum of all `p[i]`, modulo `1000000007`.

title: Best Circular Block Sum
description: `a` is arranged in a circle (the last element is next to the first). Return the largest sum of a non-empty block of consecutive elements of the circle; the block may wrap around the end and may contain at most all `n` elements.

title: Fewest Jumps To End
description: You start at index `0` of `a`. From index `i` you may jump to any index from `i + 1` to `i + a[i]`. Return the fewest jumps needed to reach the last index. Reaching it is guaranteed to be possible.

examples.explanation: The fewest number of jumps is 2.
The fewest number of jumps is 0.

constraints: 0 <= a[i] <= 1000 and the last index is reachable

title: Valley Peak Between Pattern
description: Return `true` if there are indices `i < j < k` with `a[i] < a[k] < a[j]` (a low value, then a high value, then a value strictly between them).

title: Longest Consecutive Values Run
description: Return the length of the longest set of values that appear in `a` and form consecutive integers (such as `4, 5, 6, 7`), regardless of where they sit in the array. Equal values count once.

title: Widest Container Area
description: `a[i]` is the height of a vertical wall at position `i`. Pick two different walls; together with the floor they hold water up to the lower wall's height over the distance between them. Return the largest area `min(a[i], a[j]) * (j - i)`.

title: Subarrays Divisible By K
description: Return the number of non-empty contiguous parts of `a` whose sum is divisible by `k`, modulo `1000000007`.

title: Fewest Candies For Ratings
description: Children stand in a row with ratings `a`. Give each child at least one candy, and give a child strictly more candies than an immediate neighbour with a lower rating. Return the smallest total number of candies.

title: Warmer Day Wait Total
description: `a[i]` is the temperature on day `i`. For each day, the wait is the number of days until a strictly warmer day (`0` if there is none). Return the sum of all waits, modulo `1000000007`.

title: Longest Span At Most K Letter Kinds
description: Return the length of the longest substring of `s` that uses at most `k` different letters.

title: Anagram Group Count
description: `s` is a list of lowercase words separated by single spaces. Two words are in the same group if one can be rearranged into the other. Return the number of groups.

examples.input: s = "eat tea tan ate nat bat"

constraints: s has lowercase words separated by single spaces, with no leading or trailing space

args: eat tea tan ate nat bat

title: Bracket With Star Check
description: `s` contains `(`, `)` and `*`. Each `*` may be replaced by `(`, by `)` or by nothing. Return `true` if some choice makes `s` a correctly nested bracket sequence.
constraints: s has only the characters ( ) and *

title: Digit Decoding Ways
description: Letters are encoded as numbers `A = 1, B = 2, ..., Z = 26`. A string of digits `s` can be split into pieces, each piece being one code without leading zeros. Return the number of different ways to decode `s`, modulo `1000000007`.

title: Longest Palindromic Block Length
description: Return the length of the longest substring of `s` that reads the same forwards and backwards.

examples.explanation: The longest palindromic substring has 3 letters.
The longest palindromic substring has 1 letters.

title: Expression Value With Parentheses
description: `s` is an arithmetic expression made of non-negative integers, the binary operators `+` and `-`, and parentheses, with no spaces. Return its value.
constraints: s is a valid expression: integers have no leading zeros, every operator has two operands and parentheses are balanced and non-empty

title: Zigzag Row Read
description: Write `s` in a zigzag down and up over `rows` rows (first character in row `0`, going down to the last row, then up diagonally, and so on). Return the text obtained by reading the rows one after another from the top row to the bottom row.

title: Digit String Product
description: `a` and `b` are non-negative integers written as digit strings without leading zeros (except for the number zero itself). Return their product as a digit string, without using built-in big-integer arithmetic.
constraints: a and b are digit strings without leading zeros (the string "0" is allowed)

title: Fewest Square Summands
description: Return the smallest number of perfect squares (`1, 4, 9, 16, ...`, repeats allowed) whose sum is exactly `n`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Inverse Sum Modulo
description: The modular inverse of `i` is the number `x` in `[1, p - 1]` with `i * x = 1 (mod p)`, where `p = 1000000007`. Return the sum of the modular inverses of `1, 2, ..., n`, modulo `p`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Step Set Climb Ways
description: You climb a staircase of `n` steps from the ground. In one move you climb exactly `s` steps for some `s` in `steps` (any allowed size, any number of times). Return the number of different move sequences that land exactly on step `n`, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: 1 <= steps.length <= 10 and steps are distinct values in 1..100

title: Bit Strings Without Triple Ones
description: Return the number of strings of length `n` made of `0` and `1` that do not contain three `1` characters in a row, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Square Root Floor Sum
description: Return the sum of `floor(sqrt(i))` for every `i` from `1` to `n`, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Alternating Elimination Survivor
description: The numbers `1..n` are written in a row. Repeatedly remove every second number, starting with the first one, going left to right; then repeat from the right end going right to left (removing the last number and every second number counted from the right); keep alternating direction until one number remains. Return it.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Two Congruences Smallest Solution
description: Return the smallest non-negative integer `x` with `x mod m1 = a1` and `x mod m2 = a2`, or `-1` if no such integer exists. The moduli need not be coprime.

title: Coprime Pair Count Upto N
description: Return the number of pairs `(a, b)` with `1 <= a < b <= n` and `gcd(a, b) = 1`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: One Step Life Population
description: `g` is a grid of `0` (dead) and `1` (live) stored row by row with `cols` columns. In one step, every live cell with two or three live neighbours (among its eight surrounding cells) stays live, every dead cell with exactly three live neighbours becomes live, and all other cells are dead afterwards. Cells outside the grid are dead. Return the number of live cells after one step.

examples.explanation: 3 cells are live after one step.
0 cells are live after one step.

constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 10000 and g.length is a multiple of cols; every g[i] is 0 or 1
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Cells Zeroed By Zero Lines
description: `g` is a table stored row by row with `cols` columns. Every row and every column that contains at least one `0` is entirely set to `0`. Return the number of cells equal to `0` afterwards.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 10000 and g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Diagonal Zigzag Checksum
description: Read the table `g` (stored row by row with `cols` columns) along its anti-diagonals in zigzag order: start at the top-left cell, go up-right along the first diagonal, then down-left along the next one, alternating, as in a classic diagonal traversal. If the cells are read as `v1, v2, ..., vm`, return `1*v1 + 2*v2 + ... + m*vm` modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 10000 and g.length is a multiple of cols

title: Eight Way Clear Path Length
description: `g` is a grid of `0` (clear) and `1` (blocked) stored row by row with `cols` columns. Moving between two clear cells that touch by a side or a corner (eight directions) costs one step. Return the number of cells on the shortest path from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell, counting both ends, or `-1` if there is no path.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 10000 and g.length is a multiple of cols; every g[i] is 0 or 1
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Gate Distance Total
description: `g` is a grid stored row by row with `cols` columns: `-1` is a wall, `0` is a gate and `1` is an empty room. Moving up, down, left or right through non-wall cells costs one step. For every empty room that can reach at least one gate, take the distance to its nearest gate. Return the sum of these distances (rooms that cannot reach any gate are ignored).
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 10000 and g.length is a multiple of cols; every g[i] is -1, 0 or 1
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Enclosed Cells Count
description: `g` is a grid of `0` (water) and `1` (land) stored row by row with `cols` columns. A land cell can walk to its up/down/left/right land neighbours. Return the number of land cells from which it is impossible to walk off the edge of the grid.
constraints: 1 <= g.length <= 10000 and g.length is a multiple of cols; every g[i] is 0 or 1
All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Course Order Possible
description: There are `n` courses `0..n-1`. `prereq` lists requirements as flat pairs `(a, b)` meaning course `b` must be taken before course `a`. Return `true` if all courses can be taken in some order that respects every requirement.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= prereq.length <= 200000 and prereq.length is even

title: Best Root Count
description: An undirected tree has `n` nodes `0..n-1` and `n - 1` edges given as flat pairs in `edges`. If the tree is hung from a chosen root, its height is the largest number of edges on a path from the root to any node. Return how many nodes, used as the root, give the smallest possible height.
constraints: the edges form a tree on nodes 0..n-1

title: First Cycle Closing Edge
description: An undirected graph on nodes `0..n-1` starts with no edges. `edges` lists edges as flat pairs, added one at a time in order. Return the index (counting from `0`, in terms of pairs) of the first edge whose two endpoints are already connected by earlier edges (so adding it creates a cycle), or `-1` if no edge does. A self-loop closes a cycle.

examples.explanation: The first cycle-closing edge has index 2.
The first cycle-closing edge has index -1.

constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= edges.length <= 200000 and edges.length is even

title: Fewest Bus Rides
description: Several bus lines are stored one after another in `routes`; `lens[i]` is the number of stops of line `i`, and a line runs forever through its stops in a loop (every stop of the line is reachable from every other stop of the same line with one boarding). You start at stop `s` and want to reach stop `d`. Return the fewest buses you must board, `0` if `s = d`, or `-1` if it is impossible.

examples.explanation: The fewest number of buses is 2.
The fewest number of buses is 0.

constraints: 1 <= lens.length <= 500, every lens[i] >= 1 and the lens add up to routes.length <= 100000

title: Custom Stack Replay Total
description: A stack supports three operations, given as flat triples `(type, a, b)`. Type `0` pushes the value `a` (`b` is ignored). Type `1` pops the top value and contributes it to the total (contributing `-1` if the stack is empty; `a` and `b` are ignored). Type `2` adds `b` to each of the bottom `min(a, size)` values of the stack. Return the total of all contributions, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: 3 <= ops.length <= 30000 and ops.length is a multiple of 3

title: Sliding Mean Floor Total
description: A stream delivers the values of `a` one by one. After each value, take the average of the last `k` values received (or of all values so far if fewer than `k` have arrived) and round it down to an integer (towards negative infinity). Return the sum of these rounded averages, modulo `1000000007`.

examples.explanation: The rounded averages add up to 16.
The rounded averages add up to 5.

title: Pair Sum Stream Finds
description: A collection starts empty. `ops` lists operations as flat pairs `(type, value)`. Type `0` adds `value` to the collection (duplicates are kept). Type `1` asks whether two different stored items (different insertions) add up to `value`. Return how many type-`1` operations get the answer yes.
